pages.title: The Lane and Why We Go
body: LANE AUTHORITY PAMPHLET 7-B. Please retain for your records.
The Lane is a chain of relay buoys and one jump gate, 2,040
megaklicks (Mk) from Independence Station to New Willamette.
Sixteen waypoints. Stations, landmarks, and six hazards.
The Authority wishes to stress that the Lane is marked.
> Marked is not the same as safe. Ask anyone who came back.
Why go? Cheap land, clean air, and a sky with a second sun.
Also debts. Mostly debts.
A crew is five: you, as captain, and four friends or relatives.
> Pick people you can stand. It is a long way to be wrong.
The trip takes about 155 to 185 days. Plan for 175.

pages.title: Choosing a Profession
body: Three kinds of people are licensed to fly the Lane.
CORPORATE EXECUTIVE. 1,600 cr, no useful skills. Score x1.
Money solves most problems. Spend it before they find you.
SHIP ENGINEER. 650 cr. Score x2. Repairs succeed 95% of the
time (not 80%), waste fewer spares, and drives fail half as
often.
HYDROPONICS FARMER. 400 cr. Score x3. Rations go half again
as far. Algae blooms are kinder to you.
> The Farmer scores most and survives least. Roughly one
> in three makes it. Bring a hobby that pays.
> The Executive wins three times in five, for less glory.

pages.title: Launch Windows
body: You may depart on the 1st of March, April, May, June or July.
EARLY LEAVERS meet storms near Earth: the Lunar Debris Ring
and Lagrange Shoals are rougher in March (+10%) and April (+5%).
LATE LEAVERS get a calm start, then meet the flares.
FLARE SEASON begins 15 September 2184. After that the last
three segments are mostly plasma, and the Flare Belt is worse.
Arrive before 15 September and the Authority adds 200 points.
> Most trips take 170 days. March and April are safer.
> May is a coin flip. June and July are a lesson.
> Leave early. Burn hard when it counts.
> A late start is for people who like weather reports.

pages.title: Mattie's Shopping Advice
body: Mattie Ostrander keeps the Outfitters at Independence Station.
She is right more often than you will enjoy.
ION DRIVES: three or four, at 40 cr. One drive is a wish.
RATIONS: 450 per crew member. Five crew, 2,250. Cheap: 0.30 cr.
EVA SUITS: two per crew, so ten. Ten cr each.
DRONE CHARGES: five boxes, 2 cr a box. Each scan burns five.
SPARES: one hull plate, pump and gyro. Two of each if you can.
> Heavy rations slow you a little, up to 15% at 3,000.
> Nobody ever brought too many rations. Nobody.
> Drives beyond four are spares, not speed.
> You cannot depart with zero drives, and Mattie will say so.

pages.title: Thrust and Rations
body: THRUST sets your pace. The flight computer calls it cruising.
Cruise: 22 Mk a day. No strain on the crew.
Hard burn: 27 Mk a day. Costs 2 health a day.
Overburn: 33 Mk a day. Costs 5, and drives fail twice as
often. Five days in a row and someone is exhausted.
RATIONS set how well you eat, per crew member per day.
Full: 3 rations, +2 health. Half: 2, no change.
Paste: 1 ration, -2 health. Run out entirely and everyone
loses 10 health a day.
> Overburn plus Paste is how crews become epitaphs.
> Fewer drives means slower. Three is the sweet spot.

pages.title: Weather on the Lane
body: Weather changes daily, and tends to stay as it is.
Calm and Fair: full speed, no trouble.
Unsettled: speed x0.9, small health loss, punctures likelier.
Ion fog: speed x0.7. You will get lost. Probably twice.
Solar storm: speed x0.6, health loss, ruined suits.
Flare: speed x0.5, and only near the end of the Lane.
Suits protect the crew. Fewer suits than crew means the
captain is suited first, then the rest in order.
> A storm costs about one suit in four. Count them.
> Flares hurt unsuited crew five points a day. Suited, two.
> Bring spare suits, and forgive yourself the rest.

pages.title: Stations and Trade
body: Seven stations sell goods. Each has its own prices.
Mars Relay: food at Earth prices.
Ceres Depot: cheap charges and plates.
Europa Outpost: flat food, good suits.
Titan Refinery: cheap pumps. Food is dear.
Oort Beacon: cheap gyros. No drives for sale.
Lane Terminus: cheapest food. Everything else, the most.
Stations buy back at half their price. Mattie does not.
Travelers on the road offer trades. Haggle, or do not.
> Stock up where the thing you need is cheap.
> Do not buy rations at Titan unless you enjoy regret.
> Talk to the keepers. They know the next stretch.

pages.title: Hazards and Your Choices
body: Six hazards bar the Lane. Each asks you to choose.
THREAD IT. Fly straight in. The honest option.
SHIELDS UP AND PUSH. Half the risk, but the pump may fail.
HIRE A TUG. No risk, and a fee: 25 to 120 cr, dearer in flare
season. It is the only sure way across.
WAIT FOR A BELTER PILOT. Almost safe, 10 cr plus days of
waiting. Only at the Belt Crossing and the Saturn Ring Plane.
A crossing can go wrong in five ways, from scrapes and spilled
cargo to damage, injury, and loss. Density matters.
> A damaged hull or gyro makes every hazard worse.
> Belters are slow, taciturn, and worth the coffee.

pages.title: Illness, Rest and Repairs
body: Space is not clean. Crew fall ill: dysentery, mold fever,
cryo fever, scurvy, radiation sickness and others.
Good health and full rations mean fewer deaths. Weak and
hungry crew take double the risk.
REST for 1 to 9 days. Crew recover 3 health a day, or 6 at a
station. Illness fades twice as fast.
REPAIR takes a day and a matching spare. Success is 80%, or
95% for engineers. A failed repair may still eat the spare.
Drives cannot be repaired; they stall or are lost.
> A pump out of order stops the ship. Keep a spare.
> Rest at stations. The beds there are almost beds.

pages.title: Salvage and Mini-games
body: SCAN FOR SALVAGE costs a day and five drone charges. The
drone brings back rations, and now and then a spare part.
Three or more scans in a segment halve the food found.
SALVAGE RUN: pilot the drone, fire charges, tow home up to
100 units. Rations weigh 1, spares weigh 10.
DEBRIS THREADING: when you thread a hazard, steer the ship
through the rocks. A clean run earns a bonus.
FLARE BELT: ride the plasma at the end. A clean ride earns
200 points. A crash costs a crewmate.
> You may auto-resolve any of them in Options. Poorly.
> Skipping mid-run costs a little more. Pride, mostly.

pages.title: Beacons and the Score
body: A memorial beacon marks where a crewmate was lost. Other
travelers see it. Leave a few words. Be kind to the stars.
At New Willamette, the Authority totals your journey.
Each survivor: 200 to 500, by health.
Ship 50. Drives 4, spares 2, suits 2, each.
Rations, charges and credits: a few points apiece.
Bonuses: arrive before flare season +200, nobody lost +300,
ride the wind +200. Then multiply by profession.
RATINGS: Groundling under 3,000. Spacer 3,000 or more.
Pathfinder 6,000 and above.
> Nobody has been a Pathfinder lately. Be the first.
